sentences.en: Today, his presidency has changed the rules of influence in the nation's capital, draining the old swamp, and replacing top lobbyists with a group of newcomers and former nobodies.
sentences.zh: 今天，他的总统任期改变了美国首都的影响力规则，清理了旧日的沼泽，用一群新人和曾经无名的小卒取代了顶尖游说者。

sentences.en: How to get rich in Trump's Washington.
sentences.zh: 如何在特朗普的华盛顿发家致富。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, September 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月28日星期四。

sentences.zh: 天主教会养有游说者。

sentences.en: The Boy Scouts have lobbyists.
sentences.zh: 童子军有游说者。

sentences.en: Apple does.
sentences.zh: 苹果公司也有。

sentences.en: Everybody has a lobbyiSt.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有游说者。

sentences.en: People are having impact on legislation, and indeed the people who are writing a lot of the legislation aren't people paid by special interests.
sentences.zh: 人们正在对立法产生影响，事实上，许多法律的撰写者并非那些由特殊利益集团供养的人。

sentences.en: I disagree with the notion that lobbyists don't have disproportionate influence.
sentences.zh: 我不同意游说者没有产生过大影响力的这种说法。

sentences.en: That is part of the problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在的一部分。

sentences.en: Lobbyists, donors, special interests.
sentences.zh: 游说者、金主、特殊利益集团。

sentences.en: Wall Street spent billions of dollars on lobbying and campaign contributions.
sentences.zh: 华尔街在游说和竞选捐款上花费了数十亿美元。

sentences.en: We have begun to drain the swamp.
sentences.zh: 我们已经开始清理沼泽了。

sentences.en: This is our new office in Georgetown.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在乔治敦的新办公室。

sentences.en: Blue is my favorite color.
sentences.zh: 蓝色是我的最爱。

sentences.en: Nick Confessori, who did you talk to?
sentences.zh: 尼克·孔费索里，你采访了谁？

sentences.en: So last week, I spoke to Robert Strick.
sentences.zh: 所以上周，我采访了罗伯特·斯特里克。

sentences.en: Everyone calls him Strick.
sentences.zh: 大家都叫他斯特里克。

sentences.en: Strick.
sentences.zh: 斯特里克。

sentences.en: This is an Impressionist painting of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是一幅美国国会大厦的

sentences.en: Capitol.
sentences.zh: 印象派画作。

sentences.en: He's only had an office in Washington for the last two months, let's say.
sentences.zh: 可以说，他在华盛顿开设办公室不过才两个月。

sentences.en: Oh, because he was where?
sentences.zh: 哦，因为他之前在哪里？

sentences.en: He didn't have an office.
sentences.zh: 他没有办公室。

sentences.en: An artist friend of mine did that for us.
sentences.zh: 我的一位艺术家朋友帮我们画的。

sentences.en: Strick was, until recently, a pretty minor planet among the stars of Washington lobby.
sentences.zh: 直到最近，斯特里克在华盛顿游说界的群星中还只是个微不足道的小人物。

sentences.en: And even if you were living and working in Washington in politics and government, you'd probably never heard of him.
sentences.zh: 而且就算你过去在华盛顿从事政治和政府工作，你也可能从未听说过他。

sentences.en: Yeah, so, you know, I had come to Washington in 1995.
sentences.zh: 对，所以，你知道，我是1995年来到华盛顿的。

sentences.en: Dropped out of college, worked on the Hill.
sentences.zh: 大学辍学，在国会山工作。

sentences.en: I had done the traditional trajectory of anybody who wants to work in the government affairs profession.
sentences.zh: 我走过任何想要从事政府事务专业的人的传统轨迹。

sentences.en: I had been an intern in Congress.
sentences.zh: 我曾在国会当过实习生。

sentences.en: I was a staff assistant in Congress.
sentences.zh: 我是国会的幕僚助理。

sentences.en: Worked for a couple of political consulting firMs. Did some direct mail.
sentences.zh: 在几家政治咨询公司工作过。做过一些直邮业务。

sentences.en: I had worked on the Bush campaign.
sentences.zh: 我曾在布什的竞选团队工作过。

sentences.en: I'd worked on the Dole campaign.
sentences.zh: 我曾在多尔的竞选团队工作过。

sentences.en: Did some procurement work.
sentences.zh: 做过一些政府采购工作。

sentences.en: He would help clients get contracts and sell things to agencies and the defense department.
sentences.zh: 他会帮助客户获得合同，向政府机构和国防部销售产品。

sentences.en: From there, I went and I worked at a public affairs firm.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我去了一家公共事务公司工作。

sentences.en: So I had checked all the boxes.
sentences.zh: 所以该走流程的我都走过了。

sentences.en: He had run for office once in California himself.
sentences.zh: 他自己也曾在加州竞选过一次公职。

sentences.en: He didn't win.
sentences.zh: 他没有赢。

sentences.en: I had never reached any pinnacle of anything.
sentences.zh: 我从未达到过什么巅峰。

sentences.en: I was not some guy you'd see on TV.
sentences.zh: 我也不是那种能在电视上看到的人。

sentences.en: I didn't have a massive following of people who knew who I was.
sentences.zh: 我没有一大群知道我是谁的粉丝。

sentences.en: Again, he wasn't one of the people you read about as a power player on K Street.
sentences.zh: 同样，他也不是 K 街上那些人们作为权力玩家去阅读报道的人物。

sentences.en: And to be very frank with you,
sentences.zh: 坦白讲，

sentences.en: junior is even probably too high of a term.
sentences.zh: “初级”这个词可能都算太高抬了。

sentences.en: I was a, you know, I was a nobody.
sentences.zh: 我只是个，你知道，我就是个无名小卒。

sentences.en: That all changed the night that Trump was elected.
sentences.zh: 这一切在特朗普当选的那天晚上改变了。

sentences.en: Strick happened to be friends with a bunch of folks in the Trump campaign.
sentences.zh: 斯特里克碰巧和特朗普竞选团队的一群人是朋友。

sentences.en: He had helped out on the West Coast for them.
sentences.zh: 他曾为他们在西海岸提供过帮助。

sentences.en: He had put a couple of Trump people up in his house when they were traveling.
sentences.zh: 他们在旅行时，他曾把几个特朗普团队的人安顿在自己家里。

sentences.en: He just opened his doors to Trump campaign.
sentences.zh: 他向特朗普的竞选团队敞开了大门。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's been helpful.
sentences.zh: 对，他一直很帮忙。

sentences.en: And so, you know, after the Trump victory, the thing that was, you know, that really resonated to me was that there weren't that many folks working for the
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在特朗普获胜后，让我深有感触的一点是，当时为

sentences.en: Trump campaign.
sentences.zh: 特朗普竞选团队工作的人并没有那么多。

sentences.en: You have to remember that the best people did not want to work on the Trump campaign.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，最优秀的人才根本不想为特朗普的竞选团队工作。

sentences.en: In fact, a lot of them were never Trumpers.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们中的许多人都是“绝不特朗普”派。

sentences.en: They hated him.
sentences.zh: 他们讨厌他。

sentences.en: Literally, they subscribed to this philosophy called never Trump.
sentences.zh: 字面意思上，他们信奉这种名为“绝不特朗普”的哲学。

sentences.en: They were like, this guy is a disaster.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得，这家伙简直是个灾难。

sentences.en: I don't want anything to do with him.
sentences.zh: 我才不想跟他沾上任何关系。

sentences.en: So who did he get?
sentences.zh: 那他招到了谁？

sentences.en: He got, you know, the ragtag guys, the fourth and fifth choices, people who would not have made it onto the campaigns everyone thought was going to win.
sentences.zh: 他招到的，你知道，是那些乌合之众，第四、第五梯队的选择，是那些根本无法进入大家以为会赢的竞选团队的人。

sentences.en: And then he wins.
sentences.zh: 然后他赢了。

sentences.en: And what I realized was this was going to be a whole new world of people who never were given the same sort of respect.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，这将是一个全新的人的世界，这些人以前从未受到过那种尊重。

sentences.en: I mean, I remember during the campaign that there was this black book going around where the establishment was putting in names of people who worked for Donald Trump and that
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我记得在竞选期间，有一本黑名单在流传，建制派把为唐纳德·特朗普工作的人的名字记在上面，

sentences.en: you would never get a job in Washington ever again.
sentences.zh: 这样你以后在华盛顿就再也找不到工作了。

sentences.en: And that was the kind of Washington that existed that I have, you know, for the last 20 years, I've been in Washington.
sentences.zh: 那就是过去存在的华盛顿，而我，你知道，过去20年来一直身处华盛顿。

sentences.en: And so what Donald Trump's victory did was disrupt that, that paradigm.
sentences.zh: 所以唐纳德·特朗普的胜利打破了那种，那种范式。

sentences.en: So walk me through how Strick's life and career changed after this election.
sentences.zh: 那你跟我讲讲，斯特里克的生活和职业在这场选举后发生了怎样的变化。

sentences.en: It started with a bottle of wine.
sentences.zh: 这一切是从一瓶酒开始的。

sentences.en: I'm an avid wine drinker.
sentences.zh: 我是一个狂热的葡萄酒爱好者。

sentences.en: I own a winery in Southern...
sentences.zh: 我在南部拥有一家酒庄……

sentences.en: Strick was at the Four Seasons in Georgetown, smoking a cigar in the patio, having a bottle of wine.
sentences.zh: 斯特里克当时在乔治敦的四季酒店，在露台上抽着雪茄，喝着一瓶葡萄酒。

sentences.en: And this chocolate lab comes over and starts being very friendly to me.
sentences.zh: 然后这只巧克力拉布拉多跑过来，开始对我很友好。

sentences.en: And a dog comes up and sniffs him in the crotch.
sentences.zh: 有只狗跑过来嗅他的裤裆。

sentences.en: A very friendly dog.
sentences.zh: 一只非常友善的狗。

sentences.en: And he starts talking to the dog's owner.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始跟狗的主人聊天。

sentences.en: And the owner we started talking happened to be the deputy ambassador from New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 我们开始聊天的那个主人碰巧是新西兰副大使。

sentences.en: And they're chatting.
sentences.zh: 他们在闲聊。

sentences.en: And she's like, you know, we can't get a phone call set up between the prime minister of New Zealand and the president-elect of the United States, which is one of our closest
sentences.zh: 她说，你知道吗，我们没办法安排新西兰首相和美国当选总统通电话，而美国是我们最亲密的盟友之一。

sentences.en: allies.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道该给谁打电话。

sentences.en: They don't know who to call.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道该给谁打电话。

sentences.en: They don't know who to call.
sentences.zh: 这不是因为受到什么冷落。

sentences.en: It wasn't because of any slight.
sentences.zh: 而是因为当时实在太混乱了。

sentences.en: And it was because it was just so chaotic.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，当选总统身边有许多人都没有，你知道的，权力交接的经验。

sentences.en: At this point, the president-elect had a lot of people around him who had no experience in, you know,
sentences.zh: 事实上，世界各地都在重复这种情况。

sentences.en: the transition of power.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚人不得不从高尔夫球手格雷格·诺曼那里要到一个电话号码。

sentences.en: And in fact, that was repeated all around the world.
sentences.zh: 人们甚至在问环球小姐选美大赛的选手，知不知道怎么联系上特朗普。

sentences.en: The Australians had to get a phone number from Greg Norman, the golfer.
sentences.zh: 所以当时，你有一大堆非常焦虑的国家。

sentences.en: People were asking pageant contestants in Miss Universe if they knew how to get a hold of Trump.
sentences.zh: 其中一个非常焦虑的国家就是我们的盟友新西兰。

sentences.en: And so at this time, you had a lot of very nervous countries.
sentences.zh: 所以他对她说，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And one of the countries that was very nervous was one of our allies, the country of New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 我认识几个人。

sentences.en: So he says to her, you know what?
sentences.zh: 于是他打电话给在特朗普竞选团队工作的死党。

sentences.en: I know a couple of people.
sentences.zh: 然后这位死党又打电话给几个特朗普的高层核心人物。

sentences.en: So he calls his buddy who worked in the Trump campaign.
sentences.zh: 说时迟那时快，号码就拿到了。

sentences.en: And the buddy calls a couple of Trump high command people.
sentences.zh: 然后这两位国家元首之间就通成了电话。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, a number is furnished.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And this phone call happens between two heads of state.
sentences.zh: 斯特里克对自己说，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 我一直都有雄心壮志，而且我觉得自己一直很有才华。

sentences.en: And Strick says to himself, you know what?
sentences.zh: 但现在我有了机会，因为我是那些了解如今在华盛顿举足轻重的人的人，因为他们是我的老朋友。

sentences.en: I've always had the ambition and I think I've always had the talent.
sentences.zh: 因为特朗普的竞选团队里没有多少老建制派类型的人。

sentences.en: But now I have the opportunity because I'm one of those people
sentences.zh: 所以他简直是在重写华盛顿的规则。

sentences.en: who knows the people who now matter in Washington because they're my old friends.
sentences.zh: 所以斯特里克促成了美国当选总统与新西兰首相、这两个国家之间的最初关系。

sentences.en: Because Trump did not have a lot of the old establishment types in his campaign.
sentences.zh: 那通电话是因为罗伯特·斯特里克才得以实现的。

sentences.en: So he was literally rewriting the rules in Washington.
sentences.zh: 于是新西兰方面说，好吧，那你还能做什么？

sentences.en: So Strick facilitated the initial relationship between the president-elect of the United States and the prime minister of New Zealand, between two countries.
sentences.zh: 新西兰曾是《跨太平洋伙伴关系协定》（TPP）贸易协议的签署国，而特朗普想要退出该协议。

sentences.en: That phone call happened because of Robert Strick.
sentences.zh: 他们心想，情况变化太大了，我们需要在特朗普政府的第一时间分一杯羹。

sentences.en: So New Zealand says, well, so what else can you do?
sentences.zh: 也许如果我们认识对的人，我们就能直接上第六层或第七层，因为特朗普才不管楼层顺序是什么样的。

sentences.en: New Zealand had been a signatory to the TPP, the trade agreement, and Trump wanted to pull out of it.
sentences.zh: 斯特里克说，我有个主意。

sentences.en: They're thinking a lot's changing and we need to get in on the ground floor of the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 我打算在总统就职典礼期间，帮新西兰组织一场派对。

sentences.en: And maybe if we know the right people, we can get in on the sixth floor or the seventh floor because Trump doesn't care about what order the floors are.
sentences.zh: 我会把所有我认识的那些特朗普的人，所有的副官、中士、少校，也就是特朗普世界的那些中层管理人员都请来。

sentences.en: Strick says, I have an idea.
sentences.zh: 我会把他们聚在一个房间里，然后你们就可以去推销自己了。

sentences.en: I'm going to help organize a party for New Zealand during the president's inauguration ceremonies.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: And I'm going to get all of those Trump people who I know, all of the lieutenants and the sergeants and the majors, the kind of middle management of Trump world.
sentences.zh: 他们举办了就职周期间规模最大的派对之一。

sentences.en: I'm going to get them in the room and you can make your pitch.
sentences.zh: 所有人都去了。

sentences.en: And so that's what happens.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，新西兰在特朗普的华盛顿崭露头角了。

sentences.en: They have one of the biggest parties of inauguration week.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我猜新西兰已经成了罗伯特·斯特里克的客户。

sentences.en: Everyone's there.
sentences.zh: 那场派对几周后，他们决定真正开展业务并雇佣斯特里克。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, New Zealand is on the map in Trump's Washington.
sentences.zh: 其他大使馆都在想，新西兰是怎么搞定所有那些特朗普的人的？

sentences.en: And by now, I'm going to guess New Zealand is a client of Robert Strick's.
sentences.zh: 那些家伙都是谁？

sentences.en: A few weeks after that party, they decided to go into business for real and hire Strick.
sentences.zh: 他们雇了谁？

sentences.en: And other embassies were saying, well, how did New Zealand get all those Trump people?
sentences.zh: 也许我也该雇他们。

sentences.en: Who are those guys?
sentences.zh: 尼克，让我退一步说。

sentences.en: Who did they hire?
sentences.zh: 我们总是听到“游说”这个词。

sentences.en: Maybe I should hire them.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论游说时，究竟是什么意思？

sentences.en: Nick, let me just step back for a minute.
sentences.zh: 游说者在华盛顿整天到底都在做些什么？

sentences.en: We hear the word lobbying all the time.
sentences.zh: 我觉得人们对它有一种看法，但并非真实的现实。

sentences.en: What exactly do we mean when we talk about lobbying?
sentences.zh: 游说者就是你雇来向政府陈述诉求的人。

sentences.en: And what do lobbyists actually do all day in Washington?
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着帮你安排会面、帮你拿到合同、修复你提交的某项在官僚机构某处卡壳的申请、修改一项规章、通过一项法案、起草法案，或者让国会议员关注该法案。

sentences.en: I think people have a perception of it, but not really a reality of it.
sentences.zh: 本质上，随着政府规模越来越大，他们是华盛顿特有的一类人，就像藤壶一样寄生在政府身上不断生长。

sentences.en: A lobbyist is the person you hire to make your case to government.
sentences.zh: 说客就是你雇来向政府陈述你诉求的人。

sentences.en: That can mean to get you a meeting, to help you get a contract, to fix some application you filed that got jammed up
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着帮你安排会面、帮你拿到合同、解决你提交的申请在某个官僚环节中卡壳的问题、

sentences.en: in the bureaucracy somewhere, to change a regulation, to pass a bill, to write the bill, to get Congress people to pay attention to the bill.
sentences.zh: 修改规章、通过法案、起草法案，或者让国会议员关注该法案。

sentences.en: Essentially, it is the specialized class of people in Washington that grow like a barnacle on government as government gets bigger and bigger.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，他们是华盛顿特区的一群专业人士，随着政府规模越来越庞大，他们就像藤壶一样附着在政府身上不断滋生。

sentences.en: I guess with the presumption being that if you don't have a lobbyist and you don't know how to
sentences.zh: 我想假设的前提是，如果你没有说客，你也不知道如何

sentences.en: navigate these halls of power, like, you know, your hand might be up in the air in the back of the classroom all year and nothing's happening.
sentences.zh: 在这个权力的殿堂里游走，比如，你知道，可能你一整年都在教室后排举手，却什么也没有发生。

sentences.en: You're not getting your phone calls returned.
sentences.zh: 你的电话根本没人回。

sentences.en: Yeah, you can call your congressperson.
sentences.zh: 是的，你可以给你的国会议员打电话。

sentences.en: But aside from that, almost everybody has a lobbyiSt.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，几乎所有人都有说客。

sentences.en: Every company, every trade association, labor unions have lobbyists.
sentences.zh: 每个公司、每个行业协会、工会都有说客。

sentences.en: There are even some lobbyists to advocate for the poor, although they are vastly outmatched in numbers and wealth by lobbyists for other special interests.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一些为穷人发声的说客，尽管他们在人数和财力上与代表其他特殊利益的说客相比悬殊巨大。

sentences.en: You know, it's kind of akin to what an agent in Hollywood does for his actors.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这有点类似于好莱坞经纪人为他们的演员所做的事情。

sentences.en: The same sort of thing applies in Washington, where you're really, you're being the agent for these corporations, these issues.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿也是同样的道理，你实际上是在为这些公司、这些议题充当经纪人。

sentences.en: So you're kind of the Ari Emanuel of your clients.
sentences.zh: 所以你某种程度上就是你客户的阿里·埃马纽埃尔（Ari Emanuel）。

sentences.en: Exactly, sir.
sentences.zh: 一点没错，先生。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 千真万确。

sentences.en: How much money are we talking about when we talk about money and lobbying and how much do lobbyists charge and make?
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论金钱和游说时，我们究竟在谈论多少钱？说客们的收费和收入是多少？

sentences.en: I mean, what's the scale of this?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这到底是什么规模？

sentences.en: Well, it varies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这有所不同。

sentences.en: But basically, I'd say a small boutique lobbying firm, you know, five guys and a secretary is going to charge maybe $5,000, $10,000, $15,000 a month to work on a project.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，我想说一家小型精品游说公司，你知道的，五个人加一个秘书，做一个项目大概要收5000、10000、15000美元一个月的费用。

sentences.en: That's money.
sentences.zh: 这可是一笔钱。

sentences.en: Usually every three months, you kind of re-up.
sentences.zh: 通常每三个月，你们就要续签一次。

sentences.en: The bigger firms, the ones that are, you know, merged with big PR firms or basically law firms that have lobbying practices,
sentences.zh: 那些较大的公司，也就是你知道的，与大型公关公司合并的公司，或者基本上拥有游说业务的律师事务所，

sentences.en: they have paralegals, they have big teams of researchers, they have high overhead.
sentences.zh: 他们有律师助理，有庞大的研究团队，他们的管理费用很高。

sentences.en: Those guys are more like $15,000, $20,000, $30,000.
sentences.zh: 那些家伙的收费更接近15000、20000、30000美元。

sentences.en: But look, if you were in high demand and you have the relationships that matter, you can charge $30,000, $40,000, $50,000, $100,000, a quarter million dollars.
sentences.zh: 但听着，如果你非常抢手，并且拥有重要的人脉，你可以开价3万、4万、5万、10万美元，甚至25万美元。

sentences.en: The sky's the limit.
sentences.zh: 天空才是极限。

sentences.en: And the lobbying industry as a whole is a $3 billion industry.
sentences.zh: 整个游说行业是一个价值30亿美元的产业。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So we have a team of experts that we've hired.
sentences.zh: 所以我们拥有一支我们聘请的专家团队。

sentences.en: A lot of them come from places like the Central
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人来自诸如中央

sentences.en: Intelligence Agency, the Department of Defense.
sentences.zh: 情报局、国防部等地。

sentences.en: So tell me about Strix's business today.
sentences.zh: 那么跟我讲讲斯特里克（Strix）如今的业务吧。

sentences.en: What does it look like?
sentences.zh: 它现在是什么样子的？

sentences.en: How quickly and how big has it grown?
sentences.zh: 它的发展有多快，规模有多大？

sentences.en: I think it has grown hugely.
sentences.zh: 我认为它实现了巨大的增长。

sentences.en: I think he's gone from a boutique lobbying firm with no office to speak of to something that's going to earn tens of millions of dollars this year.
sentences.zh: 我认为他已经从一家几乎没有办公室可言的精品游说公司，发展成为一家今年将赚取数千万美元的企业。

sentences.en: And you got to realize companies have lobbyists, but foreign countries also have American lobbyists.
sentences.zh: 你必须意识到，公司有说客，但外国政府也有美国的说客。

sentences.en: Private diplomacy.
sentences.zh: 私人外交。

sentences.en: His clients this year have included the Czech Republic, New Zealand, a trade association based in Korea,
sentences.zh: 他今年的客户包括捷克共和国、新西兰、一个总部设在韩国的行业协会，

sentences.en: Saudi Arabia, which is a huge spender on private lobbying in Washington.
sentences.zh: 还有沙特阿拉伯，这是华盛顿私人游说的大金主。

sentences.en: And most recently,
sentences.zh: 而最近，

sentences.en: Afghanistan, the government in Afghanistan has hired Strix to help them work through all the things
sentences.zh: 阿富汗，阿富汗政府已经聘请了斯特里克来协助他们处理所有

sentences.en: that are going to happen with this new administration, the troop surge, American reconstruction efforts there, rebuilding efforts.
sentences.zh: 将要发生的事情，包括新政府、增兵、美国在那里的重建努力以及重建工作。

sentences.en: That's a really big business.
sentences.zh: 那可是一笔真正的巨额生意。

sentences.en: In some ways, it can be bigger than corporate lobbying because the countries pay a lot more than companies.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，它可能比企业游说还要大，因为国家支付的费用比公司多得多。

sentences.en: And what we're trying to do is help countries modernize, but not westernize.
sentences.zh: 而我们正在努力做的是帮助国家实现现代化，但不是西化。

sentences.en: What I mean by that, I think the greatest extension of American power is this idea of free and fair
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为美国力量最大的延伸就是自由公正

sentences.en: elections, our First Amendment, and really the unbridled, unfettered role of capitalism within our society.
sentences.zh: 选举的理念、我们的第一修正案，以及资本主义在我们社会中真正肆意、不受束缚的角色。

sentences.en: And so what we do is...
sentences.zh: 所以我们所做的是……

sentences.en: This is a guy for whom a big client before now was the Vinyl Institute, like a trade association for vinyl manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 这家伙在此之前的一个大客户是乙烯协会（Vinyl Institute），也就是一个制造乙烯的行业协会。

sentences.en: It's a good client.
sentences.zh: 那是个不错的客户。

sentences.en: There isn't anything wrong with that.
sentences.zh: 这没什么不对的。

sentences.en: But now he's working with the president of Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 但现在他正与阿富汗总统合作。

sentences.en: He's talking to ambassadors from
sentences.zh: 他在和来自

sentences.en: Colombia.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚的大使交谈。

sentences.en: It's a much bigger stage on which to parlay his talents.
sentences.zh: 这是一个展示他才华的更大舞台。

sentences.en: You know, I use this term, which what I call the, you know, the privatization of diplomacy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我用了这样一个词，我称之为，你知道的，外交的私有化。

sentences.en: And I think what happened after the Trump victory was probably the first fresh look at the presidency,
sentences.zh: 我认为特朗普胜利后发生的事情，可能是自联邦成立以来，

sentences.en: you know, maybe since the, you know, the inception of the union and, you know, with General Washington.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许自华盛顿将军的时代以来，对总统职位最具开创性的一次审视。

sentences.en: I mean, you really had a guy coming in here, changing convention, bucking protocol, creating a new paradigm so that guys like me who didn't, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你真的迎来了一个这样的人：他打破常规，挑战礼节，创造了一种全新的范式，从而使像我这样的人——不，你知道的，

sentences.en: didn't have the fancy degrees, didn't come from, you know, the fancy law offices or the lobbying firms,
sentences.zh: 没有华丽的学位，不是来自，你知道的，那些高档律所或游说公司的人，

sentences.en: had the ability to actually bring democracy directly to the president's doorstep himself.
sentences.zh: 实际上有能力直接把民主带到总统的家门口。

sentences.en: I want to unpack this concept of the privatization of American diplomacy.
sentences.zh: 我想剖析一下美国外交私有化这个概念。

sentences.en: What does it mean?
sentences.zh: 这意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, when we talk about private diplomacy, you know, typically when we think of diplomacy, we're thinking of governments.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当我们谈论私人外交时，你知道，通常当我们想到外交时，我们想到的是政府。

sentences.en: Yeah, the United Nations.
sentences.zh: 是的，联合国。

sentences.en: United Nations.
sentences.zh: 联合国。

sentences.en: Yeah, the State Department.
sentences.zh: 是的，国务院。

sentences.en: But even in normal times, there is a whole realm of foreign policy that is conducted by multinational companies, foundations.
sentences.zh: 但即使在正常时期，也有一整个由跨国公司和基金会进行的外交政策领域。

sentences.en: Think of the Clinton
sentences.zh: 想想克林顿

sentences.en: Foundation, right?
sentences.zh: 基金会，对吧？

sentences.en: They were essentially a kind of a private diplomacy endeavor.
sentences.zh: 它们本质上是一种私人外交的尝试。

sentences.en: They were transnational.
sentences.zh: 它们是跨国性的。

sentences.en: But it's even more important now in the Trump era.
sentences.zh: 但在特朗普时代，这一点甚至更加重要。

sentences.en: Trump is essentially dismantling the State
sentences.zh: 特朗普基本上正在瓦解

sentences.en: Department.
sentences.zh: 国务院。

sentences.en: His Secretary of State, Rex Tillerson, has not bothered to appoint people to many of the chief policy jobs and diplomatic jobs in his own department.
sentences.zh: 他的国务卿雷克斯·蒂勒森（Rex Tillerson）甚至懒得为其自己部门的许多核心政策职位和外交职位任命人员。

sentences.en: It is a very small shop.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常小的机构。

sentences.en: And it's clear that the State Department under Trump is receding in importance as a player in American government.
sentences.zh: 而且很显然，在特朗普领导下，国务院作为美国政府参与者的重要性正在下降。

sentences.en: Now, some of that void is going to be filled by the military.
sentences.zh: 现在，其中一部分真空将由军方来填补。

sentences.en: And President Trump has surrounded himself with generals and ex-generals.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统身边环绕着将军和前将军们。

sentences.en: But that's also going to be filled by people like Jared Kushner, people outside the government as well, businesses, consultants, advisors, people like Robert Strick.
sentences.zh: 但这也将由贾里德·库什纳（Jared Kushner）这样的人、政府以外的人、企业、顾问以及罗伯特·斯特里克（Robert Strick）这样的人来填补。

sentences.en: They're going to do some of the work that the State Department might have done.
sentences.zh: 他们将承担一些本该由国务院完成的工作。

sentences.en: How are the prestigious, fancy, white shoe lobbying firms in Washington, how are they adapting to newcomers like Strick?
sentences.zh: 华盛顿那些声誉卓著、高档的老牌游说公司，它们是如何适应像斯特里克这样的新人的？

sentences.en: Are they happy with him?
sentences.zh: 他们对他满意吗？

sentences.en: Are they envious of him?
sentences.zh: 他们嫉妒他吗？

sentences.en: I mean, are they able to navigate their way through this the way he did?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们能够像他那样在其中游刃有余吗？

sentences.en: I think in the early months of the Trump administration, some of these guys were thrown on their backs and their clients were pretty panicked.
sentences.zh: 我认为在特朗普政府的头几个月里，其中一些人被狠狠地击倒了，他们的客户相当恐慌。

sentences.en: So one thing they did early on was they would call guys like Strick or they would call guys like Corey
sentences.zh: 所以他们早期做的一件事就是打电话给像斯特里克这样的人，或者打电话给科里·莱万多夫斯基（Corey

sentences.en: Lewandowski, who's an unregistered lobbyist who has clients and kind of helps them get stuff done in the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: Lewandowski）这样的人，他是一个未登记的说客，拥有客户并且能帮他们在特朗普政府里把事情办成。

sentences.en: They would call them for advice.
sentences.zh: 他们会打电话向他们征求建议。

sentences.en: They'd bring them in for meetings.
sentences.zh: 他们会把他们请来开会。

sentences.en: But here's the irony.
sentences.zh: 但讽刺的是这一点。

sentences.en: You've got to give President Trump something on transparency.
sentences.zh: 你必须在透明度方面给特朗普总统记上一功。

sentences.en: I mean, the idea that he's banned all his officials from going back in the lobbying business.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他禁止所有官员重操游说旧业的想法。

sentences.en: I mean...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是……

sentences.en: But he handed waivers to 100 lobbyists to come into his presidency.
sentences.zh: 但他却向100名说客发放了豁免权，让他们进入他的总统班子。

sentences.en: Well, right, but he...
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错，但是他……

sentences.en: Yeah, but the...
sentences.zh: 对，但是……

sentences.en: So I...
sentences.zh: 所以我……

sentences.en: So...
sentences.zh: 所以……

sentences.en: It turned out that Trump's world was so small that when it came time to fill his administration, he basically kind of outsourced it to industry.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，特朗普的圈子太小了，以至于到了要组建政府的时候，他基本上是把这外包给了业界。

sentences.en: So now there are over 100 former lobbyists working in his administration at pretty high levels.
sentences.zh: 所以现在有100多名前说客在她的政府里担任相当高级别的职务。

sentences.en: And they're working on the same stuff they lobbied on.
sentences.zh: 而且他们正在从事他们以前游说过的相同事务。

sentences.en: So if you're in the mining industry or the coal industry or the oil industry,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你身处采矿业、煤炭业或石油业，

sentences.en: your former guy or gal is now working in the administration.
sentences.zh: 你以前认识的那个男的或女的现在正在政府里工作。

sentences.en: So you don't have to worry about access.
sentences.zh: 所以你根本不用担心人脉问题。

sentences.en: You have it.
sentences.zh: 你已经有了。

sentences.en: The usual class of guys got back on their feet.
sentences.zh: 这群老牌家伙又重新站了起来。

sentences.en: Let me address that.
sentences.zh: 让我来谈谈这一点。

sentences.en: And I want to tell you.
sentences.zh: 我想告诉你的是。

sentences.en: So I think there's also a very negative stigma that comes on a lobbyiSt. And I don't know that most people understand that some of these congressmen
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得说客也背负着非常负面的污名。我不知道大多数人是否明白，其中一些国会议员

sentences.en: see 8,000 to 9,000 to 10,000 bills a year coming through their desks.
sentences.zh: 每年要处理8000到9000甚至10000份摆在桌上的法案。

sentences.en: And so if there's a lobbyist on one side of the issue, there's a lobbyist on the other side of the issue.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果一个议题的一方有说客，那么该议题的另一方也会有说客。

sentences.en: Lobbyists are usually the most educated on the bills.
sentences.zh: 说客通常是对这些法案了解最深的人。

sentences.en: They spend years and years and years learning the nuances of specific legislation.
sentences.zh: 他们花费了大量的时间来学习具体立法的细微差别。

sentences.en: And lobbying is nothing more than the truest extension of our ability to redress our grievances to our government.
sentences.zh: 游说不过是我们向政府表达诉求的能力的最真实的延伸。

sentences.en: So I don't have any problems with experts who are in the lobbying field going into the administration and providing their expertise.
sentences.zh: 所以我对身为游说领域专家的这些人进入政府并贡献他们的专业知识没有任何意见。

sentences.en: I think what I learned in covering this subject over the last couple of months is that Trump created chaos.
sentences.zh: 我想我在过去几个月报道这个主题时学到的是，特朗普制造了混乱。

sentences.en: He created a power vacuum.
sentences.zh: 他制造了一个权力真空。

sentences.en: And that disempowered some of the usual swamp creatures for a while.
sentences.zh: 这在一段时间内剥夺了一些常规沼泽怪物的权力。

sentences.en: But something had to fill that vacuum.
sentences.zh: 但总得有什么东西来填补这个真空。

sentences.en: I will tell you this, that, you know, without the disruption of Donald Trump, my firm doesn't exiSt. I was willing to put my family safety.
sentences.zh: 我得告诉你，你知道，如果没有唐纳德·特朗普带来的颠覆，我的公司就不会存在。我当时愿意拿我家人的安全去冒险。

sentences.en: I mean, I got to tell you,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我必须告诉你，

sentences.en: I mean, I lived in California and we put some Trump signs in our yard.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我住在加利福尼亚州，我们在院子里插了一些特朗普的牌子。

sentences.en: They were vandalized.
sentences.zh: 它们遭到破坏。

sentences.en: My home was spray painted.
sentences.zh: 我的家被喷了油漆。

sentences.en: We were threatened by our neighbors.
sentences.zh: 我们受到了邻居的威胁。

sentences.en: So, you know, there are areas in this country where being a Trump supporter wasn't, wasn't the most viable thing to do for your safety or for your family.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在这个国家的某些地区，作为一个特朗普的支持者，为了你或你家人的安全，并不是最可行的做法。

sentences.en: And so that actually emboldened me more.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上反而更让我坚定了信念。

sentences.en: — Strick seemed very defensive about, about lobbyists, about his own industry that he's now doing wildly successful in, as if he's worried about how he'll be perceived.
sentences.zh: ——斯特里克似乎对说客、对自己现在正做得风生水起的行业极力辩护，就好像他担心别人会如何看待他一样。

sentences.en: He's also very aware of the fact that despite Trump having won, being a Trump supporter is not necessarily going to ingratiate him to lots of people.
sentences.zh: 他也非常清楚这样一个事实：尽管特朗普赢了，但作为一个特朗普的支持者并不一定会赢得许多人的好感。

sentences.en: So how does he manage that?
sentences.zh: 那么他是如何处理这一点的？

sentences.en: And how does he talk about managing that?
sentences.zh: 他又如何谈论如何处理这一点的？

sentences.en: — You know, in my conversations with Strick, I find that he doesn't talk a lot about, you know, the president's big policy ideas.
sentences.zh: ——你知道，在我与斯特里克的对话中，我发现他并不怎么谈论总统的宏大政策理念。

sentences.en: — So, you know, my support of Donald Trump wasn't ideologically driven.
sentences.zh: ——所以，你知道，我对唐纳德·特朗普的支持并非出于意识形态驱动。

sentences.en: I didn't parse through all of his issue positions.
sentences.zh: 我没有去细究他所有的政策立场。

sentences.en: I didn't look at all of his positions.
sentences.zh: 我没有去看他的所有立场。

sentences.en: What I was most interested in Donald
sentences.zh: 我对唐纳德·特朗普

sentences.en: Trump was, you know, was he willing to disrupt the way Washington has done?
sentences.zh: 最感兴趣的是，你知道，他是否愿意打破华盛顿原有的行事方式？

sentences.en: And to be very frank with you, nobody else was going to give me the chance.
sentences.zh: 坦白对你说，没有其他人会给我这个机会。

sentences.en: — So I think he likes to think of Trump as a disruptor and himself as among the beneficiaries of that disruption and among the people who are
sentences.zh: ——所以我想他喜欢把特朗普视为一个颠覆者，而把自己视为这种颠覆的受益者之一，以及那些试图

sentences.en: trying to use the disruption to do some good for himself and for the world.
sentences.zh: 利用这种颠覆为自己和世界做一些好事的人之一。

sentences.en: — Nick, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: ——尼克，非常感谢。

sentences.en: — Always a pleasure, Michael.
sentences.zh: ——我的荣幸，迈克尔。

sentences.en: — Nick interviewed Robert Strick for The New Washington,
sentences.zh: ——尼克为《新华盛顿》采访了罗伯特·斯特里克，

sentences.en: The Daily's other podcast, which comes out every Saturday.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》（The Daily）的另一档播客，每周六播出。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: — The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: ——《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需提供信用卡，会怎么样？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用时，应用内的头一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看时报订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载时报应用，即可免费畅读30天。

sentences.en: — Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: — 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: — I was looking into it, and I will look into it, and I will tell you personally, I'm not happy about it.
sentences.zh: — 我当时在调查此事，而且我还会继续调查，我要亲自告诉你，我对这件事很不满意。

sentences.en: I am not happy about it.
sentences.zh: 我对这件事很不满意。

sentences.en: I'm going to look at it.
sentences.zh: 我会去关注这件事的。

sentences.en: I am not happy about it, and I let him know it.
sentences.zh: 我对这件事很不满意，我也让他知道了这一点。

sentences.en: — President Trump is publicly scolding his Secretary of Health and Human Services, Tom Price,
sentences.zh: — 特朗普总统正在公开斥责他的卫生与公众服务部部长汤姆·普赖斯，

sentences.en: for taking more than two dozen flights on private jets for both work and personal trips, which cost taxpayers more than $300,000.
sentences.zh: 因为他在公务和个人行程中乘坐了二十多次私人飞机，花费纳税人超过30万美元。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, as the president prepared to board Marine One outside the White House, he was asked if he would fire Price.
sentences.zh: 周三，当总统准备在白宫外登上海军陆战队一号时，有人问他是否会解雇普赖斯。

sentences.en: We'll see, Trump replied.
sentences.zh: “我们会着看的，”特朗普回答道。

sentences.en: — And Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell says he will support Roy Moore, the winner of a Republican
sentences.zh: — 参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔表示，他将支持罗伊·穆尔，这位阿拉巴马州共和党

sentences.en: Senate primary in Alabama, despite having backed Moore's opponent in Tuesday night's special election.
sentences.zh: 参议院初选的胜者，尽管他在周二晚上的特别选举中曾支持过穆尔的对手。

sentences.en: Moore, the former chief justice of Alabama, who famously hung the Ten Commandments in his courtroom
sentences.zh: 穆尔曾任阿拉巴马州最高法院首席大法官，他曾在法庭里挂十诫名闻遐迩，

sentences.en: and has called homosexuality a crime against nature, defeated Senator Luther Strange, a more moderate Republican backed by McConnell and a super PAC closely aligned with him.
sentences.zh: 并曾称同性恋是违背自然的罪行，他击败了参议员路瑟·斯特兰奇。斯特兰奇是一位更为温和的共和党人，得到了麦康奈尔以及与其紧密联合的一个超级政治行动委员会的支持。

sentences.en: — I think it's hard to overstate just how damaging the Alabama race was to McConnell's reputation as sort of an old-school political boss.
sentences.zh: — 我认为很难过分夸大阿拉巴马州的这场选战对麦康奈尔作为某种老派政治大佬声誉的打击有多大。

sentences.en: — I asked my colleague, Alex Burns, why Moore's election is seen as so bad for McConnell.
sentences.zh: — 我问我的同事亚历克斯·伯恩斯，为什么穆尔的当选被认为对麦康奈尔如此不利。

sentences.en: — So the value of the race, the reason why it was worth spending more than $10 million for
sentences.zh: — 所以这场选战的价值，米奇·麦康奈尔在这个超级政治行动委员会上花费超过1000万美元的原因，

sentences.en: Mitch McConnell on this super PAC was to try to send the signal that if you take on incumbent
sentences.zh: 是为了发出一个信号：如果你挑战像路瑟·斯特兰奇这样的现任

sentences.en: Republicans like Luther Strange, you are going to pay a price for it.
sentences.zh: 共和党人，你将会为此付出代价。

sentences.en: And in a lot of ways, the lesson that folks are taking out of Alabama is just the opposite, that in fact, you have a lot
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，人们从阿拉巴马州吸取的教训却恰恰相反，事实上，

sentences.en: more to gain by taking on Mitch McConnell than you have to lose.
sentences.zh: 挑战米奇·麦康奈尔所获得的利益，远比你可能失去的要多得多。

sentences.en: So if you think it's been hard for him to corral the Senate into order so far and to set the political strategy for a party led by Donald Trump, it's about to get a lot harder.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你认为到目前为止让他把参议院管好、为唐纳德·特朗普领导的党派制定政治策略是一件难事的话，那接下来只会变得更加艰难。

sentences.en: — In a statement on Wednesday, McConnell congratulated Moore and said, quote,
sentences.zh: — 在周三的一份声明中，麦康奈尔祝贺了穆尔，并引述说：

sentences.en: Senate Republicans will be as committed to keeping Alabama's Senate seat in Republican hands with Roy Moore as we were with Luther Strange.
sentences.zh: “对于让阿拉巴马州的参议院席位继续由共和党人把持，参议院共和党人对罗伊·穆尔的支持将会和我们对路瑟·斯特兰奇一样坚定。”

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天见。

sentences.en: — This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: — 本周的《威杰卡特秀》中，我们将为节日期间的招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: — Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: — 他们是那种对光线极度敏感的睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会睡到不省人事。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有什么过敏症或食物禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: — Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: — 请在《纽约时报》应用上或在你喜欢收听播客的地方寻找《威杰卡特秀》。
